title: Circuit-breaker-driven priority load-shedding + idempotency metadata for unified client timeouts
creator: Aisha Guerrero
description:
Problem: Client libraries and service endpoints currently have divergent timeout, retry and backoff defaults. During multi-region failover and sustained partial outage scenarios, we observe cascading retries from clients that defeat server-side circuit breakers and cause capacity collapse. Additionally, lack of a standardized idempotency metadata surface prevents safe request shedding and precise retry semantics.

Proposal: Implement a coordinated pattern that couples client-side timeout/backoff profiles, a lightweight idempotency metadata header, and server-side circuit-breaker driven priority load-shedding. Clients will send an idempotency key plus a priority token; servers will evaluate circuit breaker state and optionally return a canonical 'shed' response with guidance headers (retry_after, fallback_model, hedged_ok). SDKs will embed SLO-aware default timeouts and expose an opt-in hedged request helper that respects the idempotency header format. The runtime will add telemetry to attribute shed events to SLO tranche and region.

Goals:
- Prevent client retry storms from overwhelming failed regions during failover.
- Allow safe fast-fail or hedged fanout while preserving at-most-once or at-least-once semantics where appropriate.
- Make load-shedding decisions auditable and traceable to SLO tiers and circuit-breaker state.
- Provide SDK ergonomics that minimize accidental unsafe retries and make idempotency and priority explicit.

Out of scope: Full transactional idempotency store, cross-service distributed deduplication, and long-term client-side caching strategies (these will be separate follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (python, js, go) expose 'idempotency_key' and 'priority' in request constructors and default to SLO-aware timeouts
Runtime returns HTTP 429 with standardized 'X-Redwood-Shed: true' and 'Retry-After' when circuit breaker triggers for a region
Telemetry emits 'shed_event' with fields region, model, priority_tier, circuit_state in traces and metrics
Hedged request helper performs a second attempt only when 'hedged_ok' flag present in server metadata and uses idempotency key to avoid duplicate side-effects
A small canary rollout (10% traffic) shows reduced cross-region error amplification during a simulated partial outage without raising overall latency beyond 5% for P0 requests
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - design + spec: internal review of headers, SDK surfaces, and runtime hooks (complete)
Phase 1 - SDKs: add idempotency/priority fields, default timeouts, and hedged helper; unit tests + integration tests (Q1)
Phase 2 - Runtime: add circuit-breaker hook to emit 'X-Redwood-Shed' with structured headers and a region-scoped shed policy; add shed_event telemetry
Phase 3 - Canary: route 10% of production traffic with server-side shed policy enabled for non-critical models for 48h; monitor shed_event, p50/p95 latency, error amplification
Phase 4 - Gradual ramp: 10->50->100% for non-critical routes after success; restrict P0 routes until 99.95% SLI maintained
Phase 5 - SDK opt-in defaults and documentation: make hedged helper visible and document safe-idempotency patterns
metrics: SLOs affected: request_success_rate_per_region >= 99.9% for P0 under normal load
Shed events per minute (by region, model, and priority tier)
Client retry volume: proportion of retried requests that included idempotency_key
Hedged duplicate side-effect occurrences <= 0.01% of hedged attempts
implementation_notes: New headers: X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key, X-Redwood-Priority (values: p0,p1,p2,p3), X-Redwood-Hedged-Ok (true/false)

Server contract: when a circuit breaker trips for a region or model, runtime returns 429 + X-Redwood-Shed: true and Retry-After with suggested wait; upstream services should not treat 429 with X-Redwood-Shed as a hard failure for telemetry (mark as shed)
Circuit breaker policy will gain a 'priority-aware' mode where lower priority tiers are shed first; policy config stored in runtime-config and can be toggled per-customer
SDK default timeouts will be SLO-derived: client_timeout = min(per-route_slo * 0.6, 5s) for P0; exposed override for advanced users
Hedged helper: issues primary request then issues second attempt at t = 50% of remaining client_timeout if no response; uses same idempotency key and accepts server 'hedged_ok' guidance
Telemetry: add 'shed_event' and 'hedge_attempt' spans; correlate with traces and include idempotency_key hash (not raw key) for privacy
tradeoffs: Adding headers increases request surface area and requires SDK adoption; passive fallback is supported for older clients but they won't get priority shedding benefits
Hedged requests reduce tail latency but can increase load; hedged_ok flag and server-side capacity checks mitigate wasted work
Returning 429 for shed events may increase client-level error rates; we will classify shed 429s separately in dashboards to avoid alert noise
Default SLO-derived timeouts may surprise customers used to longer client timeouts; we provide clear migration docs and opt-out
test_plan: Unit tests for header serialization and SDK helper behavior across python/js/go
Integration tests: simulated region outage where server toggles circuit breaker and asserts clients receive X-Redwood-Shed and stop retries
Chaos test: inject 10% packet loss in eu-west region during canary, assert shed events increase and cross-region amplification decreases
Load test: ensure hedged attempts do not exceed 25% of baseline QPS during peak and duplicate side-effects are below threshold
Security review: verify idempotency_key hashed in telemetry and never logged in plaintext
comments: 2026-02-20 - Aisha Guerrero: Initial spec posted to Confluence (see attachments). Requested review from runtime, sdk, and SRE teams.
2026-02-25 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Asked for clarifications on how shed events interact with existing rate-limiting quotas and quota billing. Suggested 'quota-exempt-shed' flag for auditability.
2026-03-02 - Design review by Priya Nair: UX for SDK error surfaces approved; recommended explicit helper names 'hedge_safe' to reduce confusion.
2026-03-08 - Liam Chen: Prototype implemented in python SDK and runtime hook stub created in runtime repo. Draft PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/9198

2026-03-12 - Load testing results: under simulated partial outage, shed events reduced tail error amplification by 38% in canary. Observed small (3%) p95 increase for P2 routes during hedged attempts. Proceeding to extended canary per rollout plan.
